chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever eats food in his house and something falls from it, let him pick it up; and whoever eats in the desert or outdoors, let him leave it for the birds and the wild animals.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on food that falls during a meal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a nuanced legal distinction between domestic and wild environments, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maximizing resource utility within the home while practicing gratitude by sharing surplus with creation in the wild. It underscores the principle of avoiding wastefulness (israf) in private spaces while recognizing the ecological role of animals in open areas, a ruling often cited in discussions on domestic hygiene and animal rights.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who eats food in his house, so something from it falls off, so let him take it; and the one who eats in the desert, or outside, so let him leave it for the birds and the wild animals’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “

I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If one eats food in his house and pieces of food fall off, he must pick them up and eat; but if one eats food in the wilderness or outdoors he should leave such pieces for the birds and beasts.”’ (See also Ch. 48, h 15)
